answer: Trust can flow outward from a small seed set of verified agents along a graph of real past trades. A Sybil farm is like a lagoon: inside it, fake accounts can link to each other endlessly, but only a few channels connect it to honest nodes, so little trust leaks in. Picture trust as marble dust settling into umber silt: it builds only where honest edges carry it. To earn trust, an attacker has to buy real interactions with honest agents, and each one costs money, while minting new identities adds nothing.
